clue.text: Extra line put in under a prizewinning author's name

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is slipped inside the word for under

parts.note: under means below
L is the usual abbreviation for line, here an additional one

explanation.surface: An editor adds a credit line beneath the name of an award-winning writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places L inside BELOW, giving a second L. Saul Bellow won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1976.
explanation.definitionFit: Saul Bellow, the American novelist, won both the Pulitzer and Nobel prizes, so his surname names a prizewinning author.

clue.text: Todi martyr I fed to mountain beasts

indicators.note: fed to means the letter is given into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
gnus are wildebeest, crossword beasts

explanation.surface: An early Christian from Todi was thrown to animals in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed to' is the insertion signal. The surface evokes early Christians thrown to wild beasts; Ben, as in Ben Nevis, is Scottish for a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Benignus was a priest of the Umbrian town of Todi put to death for his faith under Diocletian.

clue.text: Casanova's role in The Fair Penitent

definitions.meaning: a Casanova is a womaniser, after the Venetian seducer
the seducer in Nicholas Rowe's 1703 tragedy, whose name became a byword

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The libertine character in Rowe's play gave English its word for a philanderer, the same sense as a Casanova.

clue.text: Playwright's poem this greeting is deleted from

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: is deleted from means the greeting is removed from the word this

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A dramatist's verse has had its salutation cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing HI from THIS leaves TS. Clifford Odets was the American dramatist of Waiting for Lefty; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clifford Odets was an American dramatist of the 1930s Group Theatre.

clue.text: Touchstone's dad rants comically

indicators.note: comically signals that the letters of dad rants are to be jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's jester Touchstone has a father who rages in a funny way.
explanation.walkthrough: Touchstone looks like the jester of As You Like It, but here it is a plain noun: a test of quality. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone is a criterion or benchmark against which things are measured, which is what a standard is.

clue.text: Journalist filling article with former PM's racy stories

indicators.note: filling means the journalist goes inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist
David Cameron was a British prime minister from 2010 to 2016

explanation.surface: A reporter writes up a scandalous exposé about an ex-premier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' is the insertion signal. 'Journalist' and 'article' read like newspaper talk, but give letters; the definition is Boccaccio's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's fourteenth-century collection of a hundred tales is famous for its bawdy stories.

clue.text: One breaking the net in fantastic last minute of football

indicators.note: breaking means the one forces its way into the rearranged letters
fantastic suggests wild invention, so the letters of the net in are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A striker bursts the net with a superb late goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' shuffles the three words to NINETETH, and 'breaking' places the one inside. 'fantastic' reads as praise for the goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A football match lasts ninety minutes, so the final minute of normal time is minute ninety.

clue.text: Stop reinterpreting Sartre

indicators.note: reinterpreting means reading the letters of Sartre in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Give up rereading the French existentialist.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest something is to halt it, as in arresting decline.

clue.text: Doctor No finally seen by my Italian twin in Ephesus

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of No is taken

parts.note: mio is Italian for my

explanation.surface: The Bond villain Dr No is seen with an Italian's sibling in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor No' looks like the Bond villain. 'seen by' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Comedy of Errors the twin servants are both named Dromio, one of Ephesus and one of Syracuse.

clue.text: Spice a little woman put on fruitcake

indicators.note: put on means one piece is placed after the other in this across entry

parts.note: a fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, a nut
Meg is one of the March sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women

explanation.surface: A cook adds some spice to a fruitcake, helped by a small woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' looks like the thing being spiced, but it is slang for an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of an evergreen tree, ground and used as a kitchen spice.

clue.text: Elsinore guard bristles over guarding sailors

indicators.note: guarding means the word for bristles surrounds and protects the sailors

parts.note: facial bristles make up a beard
RN is the Royal Navy, a crossword stand-in for sailors
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A sentry at Elsinore bristles with anger while watching over some seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' is the insertion signal. 'Bristles' reads as a verb of anger but is the noun; Bernardo opens Hamlet on the battlements.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernardo is one of the officers keeping watch on the castle battlements in the opening scene of Shakespeare's Hamlet.

clue.text: Fire a Creek character thus in Olivet to Calvary, perhaps

parts.note: fire as in ardour means passion
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: An ancient letter burns with feeling on the road from Olivet to Calvary.
explanation.walkthrough: Olivet to Calvary is a cantata by J H Maunder about Christ's last days; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Maunder's cantata sets the story of Christ's suffering and death, a setting of the Passion in music.

clue.text: Knight in Henry VI's grand estate drinking small beer

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: drinking means the word for estate takes in, or swallows, the abbreviation

parts.note: an estate is an area of land
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A knight from Shakespeare's history play owns a fine estate where small beer is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts S inside LAND to give LANSD. The 's of Henry VI's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir William Glansdale is a minor English knight who appears in the siege scenes of Shakespeare's Henry VI, Part One.

clue.text: Sandwich mostly left by a composer

indicators.note: left by a means the letter a departs from the shortened sandwich
mostly means all but the last letter of the sandwich word is used

parts.note: a toastie is a toasted sandwich, a British café staple

explanation.surface: Most of a sandwich has been abandoned by a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TOASTIE to TOASTI; 'left by a' removes its A, giving the composer's name. A toastie is a British toasted sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesco Paolo Tosti was an Italian songwriter famous for Victorian drawing-room ballads such as Goodbye.

clue.text: Country estate nudist's novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of estate and nudist take a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A rural property belonging to a naturist turns out to be the subject of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country estate' looks like a phrase, but 'Country' alone is the definition; 'novel' is the anagram signal, not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The USA is a nation, and a nation is a country.

clue.text: Longfellow poem does better over in Ireland

parts.note: to excel is to do better than others

indicators.note: 'in' puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A poem by Longfellow outdoes others again when read in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's 1841 poem follows a youth climbing the Alps with a banner bearing a Latin motto meaning ever higher.

clue.text: Judge supporting young man — one Potter saved from a death sentence

definitions.text: one Potter saved from a death sentence

indicators.note: supporting means in this down entry the young man sits beneath the judge

parts.note: a buck is a dashing young man
beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge

explanation.surface: A magistrate backs a youth, one that a potter rescued from execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a craftsman but means Harry Potter: in the third book Harry saves the hippogriff from execution.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippogriff condemned to death in Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban escapes with Harry and Hermione's help.

clue.text: Lewd publicity primarily endorsing fake Turin shrouds

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, or publicity

indicators.note: shrouds means the jumbled word wraps around the next piece
fake means the letters of Turin are a false version, rearranged
primarily means just the first letter of endorsing is taken

explanation.surface: Smutty advertising promotes counterfeit copies of the Turin Shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' turns TURIN into URINT, which 'shrouds' wraps round E. 'Turin shrouds' looks like the relic.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurient means having an unhealthy interest in sexual matters, and so salacious.

clue.text: School unlocked by a Dutch actor for a philosopher

parts.note: unlocked means open
Rutger Hauer was a Dutch actor, known for Blade Runner

explanation.surface: A school is opened up by a Dutch film star for a thinker to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Schopenhauer was the German pessimist thinker who wrote The World as Will and Representation.

clue.text: Seeing that, work for a river god

parts.note: as can mean since, or seeing that
an opus is a work, especially a musical one

explanation.surface: Since that is so, labour on behalf of a deity of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Asopus is the deity of a river in Boeotia, father of many nymphs.

clue.text: Jack, one in a novel who is rescued by Kep the collie

definitions.text: who is rescued by Kep the collie

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a deck of cards

indicators.note: in means the one sits inside the novel title

parts.note: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sailor, a character in a book, is saved by a sheepdog.
explanation.walkthrough: In Beatrix Potter's The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck, the collie Kep saves the duck from the fox. 'Jack' looks like a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter's naive duck is rescued from a fox by Kep the farm collie.

clue.text: Outspoken creep who wrote Zoya

indicators.note: Outspoken means a word is spoken, so its sound matters rather than its spelling

parts.note: to creep is to steal along quietly

explanation.surface: A blunt-talking sneak turns out to be the novelist behind Zoya.
explanation.walkthrough: Zoya is a 1988 novel by the American author Danielle Steel.
explanation.definitionFit: Danielle Steel, the bestselling romance novelist, is the author of the book Zoya.

clue.text: Old character, producer of Spooner's spy novel

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Dr Spooner famously did

parts.note: a rune is a character of an ancient Germanic alphabet
a maker is one who produces something

explanation.surface: An elderly figure is said to have created a thriller about espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of RUNE MAKER gives the title of Ian Fleming's James Bond book. 'Old character' looks like an old person but is an ancient letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's Moonraker is a James Bond book, a classic of espionage fiction.

clue.text: King put out sandwiches for an Austrian poet

indicators.note: sandwiches means the word for put out encloses the king between its letters

parts.note: to put someone out is to annoy them, to rile them
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch has sandwiches made for a poet from Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like deposing the king, but it means irritated. Rainer Maria Rilke wrote the Duino Elegies.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke, author of the Duino Elegies, was a poet born in Prague under the Austrian Empire.

clue.text: Dorriforth maybe holds Cecily's heart most dear

indicators.note: holds means the word for Dorriforth contains the next piece

parts.note: Dorriforth is the Catholic priest hero of Elizabeth Inchbald's novel A Simple Story; maybe marks him as an example

indicators.note: heart means the middle letters of Cecily are taken

explanation.surface: A character in a novel embraces the woman Cecily, the one dearest to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the middle two of the six letters, CI, which 'holds' places in the priest; 'dear' means costly, not beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear here means expensive, so the most dear item is the most expensive one.

clue.text: Do what Jason wanted

definitions.meaning: to do someone is slang for swindling them out of money
Jason and the Argonauts sailed to seize the Golden one from Colchis

explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the British slang sense, to cheat or swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them, and the Golden Fleece was Jason's quest prize.

clue.text: Freeing up hard cash, he survived being fired

indicators.note: Freeing up suggests loosening the letters of hard cash so they can settle in another order

explanation.surface: By releasing his funds a man escaped the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' looks like being sacked, but it means thrown into the fire: in the Book of Daniel he and two companions survived Nebuchadnezzar's furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadrach, with Meshach and Abednego, was cast into the burning fiery furnace and emerged unharmed.

clue.text: A dramatist shortened Tennyson's play

indicators.note: shortened means the dramatist's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Samuel Beckett, Irish author of Waiting for Godot, is a dramatist

explanation.surface: A playwright cut down a Victorian poet's stage drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' removes the last T of BECKETT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson wrote a historical drama about the martyred archbishop Thomas, staged by Henry Irving in 1893.
